newsitem.title: USA: Brent talk re-emerges along U.S. Gulf Coast.
newsitem.headline: Brent talk re-emerges along U.S. Gulf Coast.

text.p: Fresh talk about moving Brent into the U.S. Gulf Coast re-emerged on Monday after two cargoes were sold to Canadian refiners, traders said.

A European major was offering Brent at a discount of around 70 cents to benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing for June, equivalent to a $1.00 discount into the key Louisiana Offshore Oil Port (LOOP).
Last week, the same company sold two cargoes into the LOOP for delivery up Capline into Canada at around June WTI minus $1.00 a barrel.

Capline is a major artery linking the Gulf Coast and the Midwest. Canadian refiners west of Montreal cannot receive transatlantic cargoes directly through eastern Canada for lack of a direct pipeline link.
Among other North Sea crudes, Oseberg was offered at around WTI minus 60 cents a barrel for mid-May arrival.
The spread between WTI and Brent was around $1.70-75 cents a barrel Monday afternoon, up sharply from last week.
From West Africa, Forcados was on offer at around June WTI minus 45 cents a barrel for May 15-20 arrival. An end-May cargoes was also looking for a home around June WTI minus 65 cents, traders said.
Qua Iboe was looking for a buyer at June WTI minus 10 cents for May 15-20.
In Latin America, Bolivia's state-owned oil company has reissued a tender for 260,000 barrels of reconstituted crude oil after receiving only one offer by last Friday, trade sources said.
An Argentine company was the sole bidder, testifying to the continued oversupply in the crude market, sources said.
Yacimientos Petroliferos Fiscales Bolivianos (YPFB) will receive bids in the new tender through April 21.
The cargo loads at the Chilean port of Arica on May 7. The original tender called for loading April 15.
YPFB is holding the tender on its own behalf, as well as in the name of equity producers YPF, Perez Companc, Tesoro and Diamond Shamrock, the sources said.
